findings.quote: complete discouragement and famine: discouragement because of the panic, and famine partly because of the numbers gathered there and partly because they expected a siege
findings.problem: Greek: δυσθυμία καὶ λιμὸς ἦν ὁλοσχερής, τὰ μὲν διὰ τὸ πλῆθος, τὰ δὲ διὰ τὴν προσδοκίαν τῆς πολιορκίας. The τὰ μὲν … τὰ δέ pair covers both distress and famine together; 'because of the panic' is not a separate cause in this clause (the fear is already in διὰ τὸν φόβον earlier).
findings.proposed_fix: complete discouragement and famine, partly because of the numbers gathered there and partly because they expected a siege

findings.quote: made their way with difficulty back to Aspis
findings.problem: Greek: διέπεσον εἰς τὴν Ἀσπίδα παραδόξως. παραδόξως means unexpectedly / against expectation, not 'with difficulty'.
findings.proposed_fix: made their way, against all expectation, to Aspis

units.note: Chapter ends mid-word in Greek (ἐκ τῆς Ἀσπί|δος, continued in ch. 37); English marks it with [...], which is correct.

findings.quote: and because, too, one threatening constellation had not yet set while another was on the point of rising
findings.problem: Greek: τὴν μὲν οὐδέπω καταλήγειν ἐπισημασίαν, τὴν δ᾽ ἐπιφέρεσθαι. ἐπισημασία is a spell of stormy weather (signalled by a star's rising/setting), not a constellation; one such stormy period had not yet ended and the next was coming on.
findings.proposed_fix: and because, too, one spell of stormy weather had not yet ended while another was coming on
